basis: Dementia is persistent loss of cognitive function caused by brain dysfunction.
Congenital ineffective erythropoiesis and thrombocytopenia directly affect blood cells and marrow.
Epiphyseal dysplasia with bone aplasia, delayed ossification and joint deformities defines a skeletal disorder.
Thrombosis occupies the splenic vein; a localized venous clot does not establish a primary blood or coagulation disorder.
Intellectual disability, microcephaly and optic atrophy are defining features; short stature alone does not establish skeletal or endocrine damage.
Congenital mirror movements and corpus callosum defects reflect abnormal nervous system development.
Biliary malformation and renal tubular insufficiency are both defining; bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Neuropathy defines disease; pes cavus/split hand 2/4, ovarian insufficiency 2/5 and strabismus 4/13 support skeletal, endocrine and ocular involvement.
Congenital multiple joint contractures, sometimes with muscle fibrosis, define this heterogeneous group; neurologic disease is not universal.
Ocular myopathy defines extraocular skeletal muscle dysfunction affecting eye movement; curare sensitivity alone does not establish a neuromuscular junction disorder.
Dysplastic cystic kidneys are nonfunctional. Respiratory distress alone does not establish direct lung damage, particularly across unilateral and bilateral forms.
Skin, hair, sweat gland and dental maldevelopment define HED; ocular surface dysfunction occurs in 30-79%. Asthma is separate; immunodeficiency is a rare subtype.
Congenital hypotrichosis and progressive macular degeneration define the syndrome; skeletal dysplasia occurs in only 5-29%.
Keratinizing epithelium accumulates destructively in the middle ear or mastoid; its epithelial composition does not establish separate skin involvement.
Bacterial infection defined by Acinetobacter; the umbrella concept specifies no consistently affected anatomical organ.
Infantile storage disease with neurodegeneration and dysostosis; blindness 80-99%. Hearing loss 80-99% and cardiomyopathy 30-79% omitted by cap; organomegaly alone does not prove dysfunction.
An inherited distal skeletal myopathy; TARDBP association alone does not justify adding motor neuron or other neurologic disease.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; supplied HPO reports aortic aneurysm, dental malocclusion and craniosynostosis each at 30-79%, supporting vascular, oral and skeletal involvement.
Anterior horn motor neuron disease causes denervation and amyotrophy; skeletal deformities have no established frequency here.
Inherited myopia is an ocular growth and refractive disorder.
Craniofacial dysostosis, alopecia and hypogonadism define disease; CNS defects/ID 80-99%. Ocular defects (30-99%) and dental anomalies (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Classic form predominates: hepatic injury ~80%, neurodevelopmental impairment >30%, cataracts ~30%; cataracts also define galactokinase deficiency. Frequencies vary by subtype.
Defined by cardiac structural, contractile and electrical dysfunction; cirrhosis is the underlying separate liver disease, not damage caused by this cardiomyopathy.
ZC4H2-related neurodevelopmental disease with defining arthrogryposis and contractures; other listed organ findings lack evidence of common direct damage.
Chronic right middle lobe atelectasis and pneumonitis directly affect the lung; infection or immune-mediated disease is not required.
